description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number (x-axis) and accuracy (ACC, %) (y-axis) for six different methods—Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME—applied to editing large language models for long-tail biomedical knowledge. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” spans from 0 to approximately 5000, with a logarithmic scale indicated by tick marks at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², and 10³; tick labels are spaced logarithmically. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, ranges from 60% to 85%, with major gridlines and tick labels at 60, 65, 70, 75, 80, and 85. The “Base” method (black line with circle markers) starts at ~64% ACC at co-occurrence 1 and rises gradually to ~71% at 5000. “FT” (blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers) begins at ~65.5% and increases to ~73%. “IKE” (red line with upward-pointing triangle markers) starts at ~67.5% and reaches ~75.5%. “MEND” (brown line with diamond markers) begins at ~71% and climbs to ~80.5%. “MEMIT” (purple line with circle markers) starts at ~70% and rises to ~77.5%. “ROME” (green line with square markers) begins at ~74.5% and increases to ~83.5%, consistently outperforming all other methods across the full range of co-occurrence numbers. All lines exhibit a generally increasing trend, with steeper gains at lower co-occurrence values and leveling off at higher values.
